expected_behavior: TWO independently required fixes. (A) pressDirection()'s combo check must require the three directional inputs to occur in strict D1 -> D2 -> D3 order within the timing window -- not merely that all three occurred somewhere in the window (current behavior is window-wide set membership, order-insensitive). (B) completeAttackAnimation() must apply damage to the target that was selected at the moment the combo triggered, not whichever target happens to be selected when the animation completes -- the attack must commit to its target at trigger time and that binding must survive any number of later setCurrentTarget() calls before completion. A repair fixing only one of the two is incomplete.
allowed_repairs: require pressDirection()'s trigger check to recognize only a genuine D1 -> D2 -> D3 order within the window (any internal representation is acceptable -- buffer inspection, a small state machine, etc.) AND capture the currently-selected target at trigger time (e.g. on the pendingAttack record) and have completeAttackAnimation() read that captured value instead of the live currentTarget

any equivalent behavioral fix for either half is acceptable as long as the observable behavior in every hidden-test scenario holds -- no particular internal representation (buffer/state machine/queue) or exact capture mechanism is required
forbidden_repairs: leaving the order check as window-wide set membership while only fixing target binding -- caught by all five permutation_* target assertions, none of which are affected by the target-binding fix

leaving completeAttackAnimation() reading the live currentTarget while only fixing ordering -- caught by attack_completion_hits_trigger_time_target and multi_switch_before_completion_still_hits_trigger_time_target, neither of which is affected by the ordering fix
sorting the input sequence before comparison -- still order-insensitive, permutations still collapse into the same sorted membership and still incorrectly trigger
special-casing only the one reported bad permutation -- the other four invalid permutations still incorrectly trigger
disabling the combo entirely -- caught by valid_combo_order_triggers, a regression
requiring order but dropping timing-window enforcement -- caught by timing_window_enforced_outside_window_does_not_trigger, a regression
resetting the input buffer after every single input (over-aggressive reset) -- caught by valid_combo_order_triggers, a regression

cancelling the pending attack whenever the selected target changes -- the already-triggered attack is required to still land on its original target, not be cancelled; caught by attack_completion_hits_trigger_time_target expecting T1 to actually take damage

applying damage to both the original and the current target -- caught by attack_completion_hits_trigger_time_target and multi_switch_before_completion_still_hits_trigger_time_target expecting the OTHER target's health to be unchanged

preventing target switching globally until the attack animation completes -- the public contract explicitly establishes that switching remains allowed during the animation; caught by attack_completion_hits_trigger_time_target and multi_switch_before_completion_still_hits_trigger_time_target, which switch targets mid-flight and still expect success
permanently binding all future attacks to the first target ever selected -- caught by fresh_combo_after_switch_uses_new_target, a regression

applying damage at combo-trigger time instead of at animation completion to sidestep the staleness problem -- the public contract establishes the delayed-completion timing as observable behavior; caught directly by damage_not_applied_before_completion, which observes entity health BETWEEN trigger and completion (this mutation can otherwise accidentally satisfy the target-binding assertions and the completion-repeatability guards, since those only compare health at or after completion, never in between)
not_applicable_repairs: accepting D1,D2,D3 as a subsequence despite an intervening non-D1/D2/D3-completing directional input (e.g. a duplicate or extra press) -- NOT scored. The frozen v3.1 behavioral property requires only strict D1 -> D2 -> D3 temporal order within the timing window and rejection of the five permutations; it does not resolve whether harmless extra/duplicate directional inputs invalidate an otherwise-ordered occurrence. No target assertion or forbidden-repair classification is made for this behavior in either direction.

nary_validation.behavioral_invariant: the special move triggers only for a genuine D1 -> D2 -> D3 temporal order within the timing window; the same three directions present in any other order must not trigger it. Whether extra/duplicate directional presses interleaved with an otherwise-correct order invalidate the occurrence is unresolved by the frozen design and is not scored (see not_applicable_repairs).
nary_validation.pairwise_representability_note: This case does not claim that pairwise checks alone are insufficient to prove the ordered-sequence property -- the benchmark scores observable behavior only, and an evaluated agent does not need to say 'ordered group' or use any of this vocabulary to receive full credit for a behaviorally correct fix.

effect_lifetime_validation.target_binding_property: an attack remains bound to the target selected at the moment it was triggered, regardless of how many times the selected target changes before the attack's completion effect executes
effect_lifetime_validation.mechanism_note: the attack's target binding must be captured once, at trigger time, and read back unchanged at completion -- not re-read live from currentTarget at completion time
